Using \(2n\equiv -1\pmod{2n+1}\), we get
\[
(2n)^2\equiv 1,\qquad (2n)^4\equiv 1 \pmod{2n+1}.
\]
Thus
\[
4n^2\equiv 1,\qquad 16n^4\equiv 1 \pmod{2n+1}.
\]
So
\[
16(n^4+n^2)\equiv 1+4=5 \pmod{2n+1}.
\]
Since \(\gcd(16,2n+1)=1\), the divisibility \(2n+1\mid n^4+n^2\) is equivalent to
\[
2n+1\mid 5.
\]
For positive \(n\), this gives \(2n+1=5\), so \(n=2\).

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
